raw_case_text:
Congenital brucellosis was diagnosed in patients 1 and 2, who were 3-month-old twins (Technical Appendix Table). They were prematurely delivered by cesarean section on July 6, 2012, at the Provincial Maternity and Child Care Center (Guangzhou, China). The boy (patient 1, Apgar score 9-10/1-10 min) had a birthweight of 2.3 kg, and the girl (patient 2, Apgar score 9-10/1-10 min) had a birthweight of 1.8 kg. They received standard care for preterm neonates at the hospital. They were discharged once their weight reached 2.5 kg; this happened for patient 1 at 3 weeks of age and for patient 2 at 4 weeks of age (July 29 and August 3, 2012, respectively).
On October 2, 2012, the boy was examined at the hospital for irregular fever up to 39 C. On October 9, he was readmitted to the hospital with a fever of 38 C and weight of 5.0 kg. Chest radiograph showed signs of increased bronchovascular shadows. Mezlocillin sodium and sulbactam sodium (4:1) and ribavirin were administered, but the patient did not improve. On the same day, the girl had a cough and low-level fever (37-37.5 C) but was not hospitalized. On October 16, B. melitensis was isolated from a blood culture from patient 1, in whom brucellosis with alveobronchiolitis, abnormal hepatic function, and moderate anemia were initially diagnosed when he was 3 months and 10 days of age.
On October 17, the twins were transferred to an infectious disease hospital, where they had extensive physical and laboratory examinations (Table 1). During 57 days of hospitalization, the boy received general and specific therapies for brucellosis. Brucellosis and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency were diagnosed in the girl, and she received appropriate treatment. At the time of discharge (December 12), the twins were well and without fever. They left the hospital for home care, which was supervised by a local general practitioner who provided rifampin and sulfamethoxazole for up to 6 weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: Three-month-old premature twins presented with irregular fever up to 39 °C, low-grade fever (37-37.5 °C), and cough.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The twins were delivered prematurely by cesarean section on July 6, 2012, and discharged after reaching 2.5 kg weight. On October 2, 2012, the male twin developed irregular fever up to 39 °C and was readmitted on October 9 with fever of 38 °C and respiratory distress unresponsive to mezlocillin/sulbactam and ribavirin. Concurrently, the female twin developed cough and low-grade fever (37-37.5 °C). On October 17, both infants were transferred to an infectious disease hospital for specialized evaluation and care.
subjective.past_medical_history: Premature delivery via cesarean section at 34 weeks and 2 days' gestation. Birth weights: 2.3 kg (twin 1, boy) and 1.8 kg (twin 2, girl); Apgar scores 9-10 at 1 and 10 minutes. Preterm neonatal care received until discharge at 3 weeks (boy) and 4 weeks (girl) of age upon reaching 2.5 kg. No known direct animal contact.
subjective.review_of_systems: Cough and low-grade fever in twin 2; irritability, fever, and respiratory symptoms in twin 1. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Twin 1 (boy): temperature 38-39 °C, body weight 5.0 kg; signs of respiratory distress. Twin 2 (girl): temperature 37-37.5 °C, cough. Other detailed physical findings not documented.
objective.routine_investigations: Twin 1: Chest radiograph showed increased bronchovascular shadows consistent with alveobronchiolitis; laboratory tests showed abnormal hepatic function and moderate anemia. Twin 2: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency identified.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Congenital brucellosis due to Brucella melitensis in twin infants, complicated by alveobronchiolitis, hepatic dysfunction, and moderate anemia in the male twin, and coexisting glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency in the female twin.
Confirmation: Blood culture in twin 1 isolated Brucella melitensis on October 16.
Treatment & Outcome: Initial empiric therapy with mezlocillin/sulbactam (4:1) and ribavirin failed. Following diagnosis, both twins received targeted anti-brucellosis therapy during a 57-day hospitalization, followed by outpatient oral rifampin and sulfamethoxazole for up to 6 weeks. At discharge, both infants were afebrile, clinically well, and had fully recovered.
